Responsibilities

Work with the CPU design team to identify critical paths and timing bottlenecks across IP development, enabling accurate trade-off between the various performance metrics of the designs (frequency, IPC, power, area)
Produce Power/Performance/Area figures and help CPU micro-architecture improvement
Analyse existing tools for enhancements/automation, alongside trialling new tools

Qualification

Represents the skills you have

Find out how your skills align with this job's requirements. If anything seems off, you can easily click on the tags to select or unselect skills to reflect your actual expertise.

CPU Physical ImplementationLogic SynthesisFloorplanningPower PlanningClock Tree SynthesisPlace and RoutePower, Performance, and Area OptimizationCMOS DesignCPU MicroarchitectureUnified Power Format (UPF)Design-for-Test (DFT)PythonPerlTclUNIX/LinuxGitWorkload SchedulingFrench

Required

Hold (or are on track to hold) a University degree by the programme start date. This can be Bachelors, Masters or PhD in Electronic Engineering or Computer Science
Candidates with alternative degrees will also be considered depending on experience
Exposure to synthesis/floor-planning/power planning, clock tree, place and route tools and techniques through school projects or internships
Understanding of Power versus Performance versus Area tradeoff in typical CMOS design
Knowledge of CPU micro-architecture concepts (cache, MMU, pipeline…)
Ability to schedule own workload and plan tasks
Good interpersonal skills

Preferred

Knowledge of power domain management through UPF (2.0 and onwards)
Basic understanding of DFT techniques
Experience developing scripts (Python, Perl, Tcl …) for automation purpose
Working in UNIX/Linux environment, with bug tracking and source code control systems, especially GIT
Able to work in French and in English

Benefits

Visa sponsorship support is also available for candidates who require it.
Relocation support is available for domestic moves within the country and regional moves within Europe.
Clear opportunities to progress within the salary range at Arm.
Two formal progression windows each year, with mid-year and year-end reviews recognising your growth.
“Grad-teach-Grads” workshops, guest speaker series, and social events.
Opportunity to join the Graduate Committee to further develop planning, networking, and coordination skills.
Invitation to the Global Graduate Conference (GGC), an annual event where graduates hear from executive leaders and guest speakers and build lasting connections.
Hybrid working patterns determined by groups/teams based on the work and the team’s needs.
